prompt: Which physical quantity has the derived SI base units $\text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-3}$?

answer.explanation: Power is defined as work done per unit time (P = W/t). Dividing the base units of work (kg m^2 s^-2) by seconds yields kg m^2 s^-3 (the watt).

distractor_explanations: Incorrect. Force has base units kg m s^-2.
Incorrect. Work has base units kg m^2 s^-2.
Correct. Power P = W/t has base units (kg m^2 s^-2) / s = kg m^2 s^-3 (watt).
Incorrect. Pressure has base units kg m^-1 s^-2.
hints: Compare the power of s^-3 to the units of work (s^-2).
Which quantity is the rate of change of work with respect to time?
solution: Work has base units kg m^2 s^-2. Dividing by time (s) to get the rate of work done gives: (kg m^2 s^-2) / s = kg m^2 s^-3. This is the unit of power (the watt). Option C is correct.
teacher_walkthrough: Reverse lookup: identify quantity from given base units.
Encourage students to inspect the time power: s^-2 (force/energy) vs s^-3 (power).
